cards.text: This is a Maskil of Asaph, a worship leader in David's day (1 Chronicles 16:5), and he opens like a man tapping the mic: “Give ear, O my people, to my instruction; listen to the words of my mouth.” Then he says he'll open his mouth in parables and speak of things hidden from the beginning.

cards.question: Asaph is about to share things hidden from the beginning. How did these things reach him and his people?
Asaph says his people will keep these stories hidden from their children.

cards.text: Instead, they'll declare to the next generation the praises of the LORD, His might and the wonders He has performed. Nobody's shoving THIS in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and trust me, I spent years back there.

God set up a testimony in Jacob and a law in Israel, and He commanded the fathers to teach them to their children. The goal is that the coming generation knows them, even children not born yet, and tells THEIR children too, like a relay race where nobody's allowed to drop the baton.

cards.question: Why does God want every generation passing these things down?

answers.text: So they'd put their confidence in God
So the nations would fear them
So they'd never need a king

cards.question: Asaph says the next generation won't be like their fathers. How does he describe those fathers?

cards.text: Their hearts weren't loyal to God, and their spirits weren't faithful to Him. Picture a recipe card with a note at the bottom: “Whatever you do, don't make it the way THEY did.”
Then Asaph brings up the archers of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes (Numbers 1:32-33). Bows in hand, day of battle, here we go… and they turn back.

cards.question: Right after the archers of Ephraim turn back, Asaph says they refused to live by God's law.
Asaph says the archers of Ephraim ___ the wonders God had shown them.

cards.text: Then Asaph goes back to the land of Egypt. There, in the region of Zoan, God worked wonders right in front of their fathers.

cards.question: Asaph says God dried up the sea with the sun so His people could cross.

cards.text: “He split the sea and brought them through; He set the waters upright like a wall.” WATER, standing UP, like a WALL, friend, and I can't get a ball of dough to stand up for ten seconds.

cards.question: Asaph also tells how God led His people. What did God lead them with?

answers.text: A cloud by day and fire by night
An angel walking ahead of them
A star shining in the east

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, God split the rocks, and out came ___.

cards.text: After all those wonders, the very next line starts with “But.” They kept right on sinning, rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

cards.question: In the desert, the people willfully tested God by ___ the food they craved.

cards.text: They spoke against God, saying, “Can God really prepare a table in the wilderness?” Friend, they're asking that about the God who split the SEA.

cards.question: The people admit God struck the rock and water gushed out. What do they doubt He can do next?
When the LORD heard what the people said, He was filled with ___.
Asaph says God's anger flared because the people did not believe God or rely on His salvation.

cards.text: Yet look what God does next. He commands the clouds above and opens the doors of the heavens.

cards.question: What does God rain down on the people from the open doors of the heavens?

cards.text: Asaph says, “Man ate the bread of angels; He sent them food in abundance.” I've stamped a LOT of cookies, friend, and not one batch ever got called the cookies of angels.

cards.question: God stirs up the east wind and drives the south wind by His might. What does He rain down on the people like the sand of the sea?
Asaph says God brought the birds down far outside the camp.

cards.text: So they ate and were well filled, for He gave them what they craved. Ask for one cookie, get buried under the WHOLE batch.
Before they had filled their desire, with the food still in their mouths, God's anger flared against them.
He put to death their strongest and subdued the young men of Israel. This part is heavy, friend.
In spite of all this, they kept on sinning, and despite His wonderful works, they did not believe. So He ended their days in futility and their years in sudden terror.

cards.question: When God slew them, the people would ___ Him.

cards.text: They repented, and they remembered that God was their Rock, that God Most High was their Redeemer.
But they deceived Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues.

cards.question: Asaph says the people's hearts were loyal when they turned back to God.
The people's hearts are disloyal to God. What does God do?

answers.text: Waits for them to bring an offering
Sends a prophet to warn them

cards.question: Asaph says God often restrained His anger and did not unleash His full wrath.
What does Asaph say God remembered about His people?

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Asaph is NOT done telling this one.
